head.title: Apache Axis2 OpenAPI REST Services User's Guide

body.h1: Apache Axis2 OpenAPI REST Services User's Guide
body.p: What is OpenAPI? OpenAPI (formerly known as Swagger) is an industry-standard specification for describing REST APIs. It provides a machine-readable format that precisely defines your API endpoints, request/response schemas, authentication methods, and error handling. Think of it as a contract that documents exactly how your REST API behaves, enabling automatic client code generation, interactive testing, and comprehensive documentation that stays in sync with your actual implementation.

Why use OpenAPI? For developers, OpenAPI eliminates the tedious manual work of writing and maintaining API documentation, reduces integration errors through precise specifications, and enables powerful tooling ecosystems. Your frontend developers get auto-generated TypeScript clients, your QA teams get interactive testing interfaces via Swagger UI, and your DevOps teams can generate monitoring configurations automatically. Most importantly, OpenAPI specifications serve as the single source of truth for your API, preventing the documentation drift that plagues many projects.

This guide demonstrates how to create OpenAPI 3.0.1 documented REST services with Apache Axis2, providing a drop-in replacement solution for existing REST backends. It includes comprehensive examples for financial services, data management systems, and enterprise applications with OpenAPI specification support and interactive Swagger UI documentation!

The guide shows how to build REST services that can seamlessly replace existing backends (Spring Boot, Express.js, etc.) while maintaining API compatibility for frontend applications such as Excel Add-ins, React apps, and TypeScript clients.
Introduced in Axis2 2.0.1: OpenAPI 3.0.1 integration with automatic specification generation from deployed services, Swagger UI support, and an MCP tool catalog.

More documentation about Axis2 REST support can be found in the Pure JSON Support documentation and JSON User Guide. For modern enterprise features including Bearer authentication, advanced security schemes, and comprehensive configuration options, see the OpenAPI Advanced User Guide.

This user guide is written based on the Axis2 Standard Binary Distribution. The Standard Binary Distribution can be directly downloaded or built using the Source Distribution. If you choose the latter, then the Installation Guide will instruct you on how to build Axis2 Standard Binary Distribution using the source.

The source code for this guide is a small sample application demonstrating an OpenAPI-documented REST authentication service. The data, calculation and Excel examples later in this guide are illustrative patterns for your own services; they are not part of the sample.

Please note that Axis2 is an open-source effort. If you feel the code could use some new features or fixes, please get involved and lend us a hand! The Axis developer community welcomes your participation.
Let us know what you think! Send your feedback to "java-user@axis.apache.org". (Subscription details are available on the Axis2 site.) Kindly prefix the subject of the mail with [Axis2].

Since 2.0.1, Axis2 provides OpenAPI 3.0.1 integration designed for enterprise REST services and drop-in backend replacement scenarios. The OpenAPI module generates the specification from the services deployed in Axis2, and lets you adjust the generated document programmatically.

ul.li: Automatic Generation: The specification is generated by introspecting the deployed Axis2 services; an OpenApiCustomizer can modify the generated document
Interactive Documentation: Swagger UI (served at /swagger-ui) for API testing and exploration
Standard Endpoints: OpenAPI specifications served at /openapi.json and /openapi.yaml, and an MCP tool catalog at /openapi-mcp.json
CORS Headers: The specification and Swagger UI responses carry permissive CORS headers for browser-based tools
Service Discovery: Automatic detection of REST-enabled Axis2 services
Drop-in Compatibility: Designed to replace existing REST backends without frontend changes

body.p: The OpenAPI module always generates the specification from the deployed services; it does not serve a hand-written schema file in place of the generated one. To change the generated document (add servers, security schemes, descriptions or extra schemas), implement org.apache.axis2.openapi.OpenApiCustomizer and register it on the OpenApiConfiguration. See the OpenAPI Advanced User Guide for details.
The Axis2 OpenAPI integration is specifically designed for backend replacement scenarios:

ul.li: API Compatibility: Maintain existing endpoint paths, request/response formats
Authentication Patterns: Support for custom headers and standard Bearer tokens
Frontend Support: Compatible with TypeScript clients, Excel Add-ins, React apps
Migration Path: Gradual service-by-service replacement without breaking changes

body.p: This user guide explains how to write and deploy OpenAPI-documented REST services using Axis2, and how to replace existing backends while maintaining frontend compatibility.
All the sample code mentioned in this guide is located in the "modules/samples/swagger-server" directory of Axis2 standard binary distribution.
The sample provides an OpenAPI-documented authentication service, together with a reference OpenAPI contract for a larger financial API (src/main/resources/openapi/financial-api-schema.json).

Testing the Sample: The swagger-server sample includes comprehensive unit tests for all service components and models. To run the tests, navigate to the sample directory and execute mvn test. The test suite covers authentication flows, data validation, JSON serialization/deserialization, and service method functionality. Individual test classes can be found in src/test/java/org/apache/axis2/samples/swagger and provide excellent examples of how to test REST services with custom authentication patterns and complex data models.
The guide demonstrates how to create secure, OpenAPI-documented REST services using real-world patterns commonly found in financial services and data management applications.
The swagger-server sample contains one service:

ul.li: AuthenticationService: POST /bigdataservice/login, login with custom token generation. For demonstration it accepts any well-formed email address with the credentials demo.

body.p: The reference contract financial-api-schema.json also describes /bigdataservice/funds/summary, /bigdataservice/assets/calculate and /bigdataservice/user/*; these are not implemented by the sample. The data, calculation and Excel services shown below are illustrative patterns for your own services.
The AuthenticationService demonstrates token-based authentication using OpenAPI 3.x annotations (from io.swagger.v3.oas.annotations):
An illustrative data service with authenticated endpoints (not part of the sample):

Note: Axis2's OpenAPI integration uses io.swagger.v3.oas.annotations (OpenAPI 3.x), not the older Swagger 1.x annotations (@Api, @ApiOperation, @ApiParam). See the
Swagger 2.x annotation guide for the full reference.

Axis2 supports multiple JSON libraries — Moshi, Gson, and a streaming formatter — each with standard and HTTP/2-enhanced variants. Select the library by choosing the corresponding message builder and formatter classes in axis2.xml. The examples below use Moshi's @Json annotation; Gson provides equivalent functionality with @SerializedName:
To enable OpenAPI documentation, place the openapi module archive (openapi-<version>.mar, built from axis2-openapi) in the repository's modules directory and engage it in your axis2.xml:
body.pre: <module ref="openapi" />
body.p: The module generates the specification, but it does not register any servlet itself. The documentation endpoints are served by delegating to the module's SwaggerUIHandler from a servlet mapped at /openapi.json, /openapi.yaml, /swagger-ui and /openapi-mcp.json. The Axis2 Spring Boot Starter registers such a servlet automatically; the springbootdemo-tomcat11 sample shows a hand-written OpenApiServlet that calls OpenApiModule.getSwaggerUIHandler(configContext).

Configuration is read from an openapi.properties file on the classpath, and any of the same keys may be overridden with Java system properties (for example -Dopenapi.title=...). The supported keys are:

ul.li: openapi.title, openapi.description, openapi.version, openapi.termsOfServiceUrl: API information in the generated specification
openapi.contact.name, openapi.contact.email, openapi.contact.url: contact information
openapi.license.name, openapi.license.url: license information
openapi.serverBaseUrl: absolute URL to publish in servers[].url; by default a relative URL is published rather than one derived from the request
openapi.prettyPrint: pretty-print the generated JSON
openapi.swaggerUi.enabled: enable the Swagger UI page (default: true)

openapi.swaggerUi.version, openapi.swaggerUi.integrity.bundle, openapi.swaggerUi.integrity.standalonePreset: the Swagger UI version loaded from the CDN (default 5.32.13) and the Subresource Integrity hashes for a non-default version
openapi.resourcePackages, openapi.readAllResources: which resource classes to scan
openapi.ignoredServices, openapi.ignoredOperations, openapi.ignoredRoutes: comma-separated services, operations (ServiceName/opName or opName) and path patterns to leave out of the specification

body.p: The module.xml inside the .mar also accepts the parameters title, version, description, prettyPrint, supportSwaggerUi and propertiesFile (the name of an additional properties file to load).
The OpenAPI REST services are designed for seamless integration with existing frontend applications. Here are examples showing drop-in compatibility patterns:
Login request maintaining existing frontend patterns:
body.pre: curl -v -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -X POST \ --data '{"email":"user@company.com","credentials":"demo"}' \ http://localhost:8080/axis2/services/authService/login
body.p: Response format compatible with existing frontends:
Data requests using a custom bigdataToken header (maintaining frontend compatibility). This and the following examples illustrate patterns for your own services; the sample does not implement them:
body.pre: curl -v -H "bigdataToken: eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..." \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -X POST \ --data '{"marketId":"MKT001","includeHistory":true}' \ http://localhost:8080/axis2/services/dataService/marketSummary
body.p: Where the response maintains existing data structure:
Financial calculation requests with custom authentication:
body.pre: curl -v -H "bigdataToken: eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..." \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -X POST \ --data '{"calculationType":"netPresentValue","cashFlows":[100,200,300],"discountRate":0.05}' \ http://localhost:8080/axis2/services/dataService/financialCalculation
body.p: Financial calculation response format:
Excel Add-in compatibility with function specification endpoints:
body.pre: curl -v -H "bigdataToken: eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..." \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -X GET \ http://localhost:8080/axis2/services/excelService/functionSpecs

Once deployed, the OpenAPI integration provides multiple ways to access API documentation:
Access the interactive API documentation at the path where the OpenAPI servlet is mapped, for example:
body.pre: http://localhost:8080/axis2/swagger-ui
body.p: The Swagger UI provides:

ul.li: Interactive Testing: Try API endpoints directly from the browser
Authentication Support: Test with custom headers and tokens
Request/Response Examples: See expected data formats
Schema Documentation: Detailed model and parameter information

body.p: Access the raw OpenAPI specifications:
body.pre:
# JSON format http://localhost:8080/axis2/openapi.json
# YAML format http://localhost:8080/axis2/openapi.yaml
# MCP tool catalog http://localhost:8080/axis2/openapi-mcp.json
body.p: The specification endpoints send CORS headers for frontend integration and can be used by:

ul.li: Code Generation: Generate TypeScript/JavaScript clients
API Testing: Import into Postman, Insomnia, or similar tools
Documentation: Generate static documentation or integrate with docs systems

body.p: This section provides step-by-step guidance for replacing existing REST backends with Axis2 OpenAPI services while maintaining frontend compatibility.
Follow this approach for seamless backend replacement:

ol.li: API Analysis: Document existing endpoints, request/response formats, and authentication patterns
Service Implementation: Create Axis2 services matching existing API contracts
Configuration: Engage the OpenAPI module and compare the generated specification with your existing schema, adjusting it with an OpenApiCustomizer where needed
Testing: Validate compatibility with existing frontend applications

body.p: Handle common frontend integration patterns:
Validate drop-in compatibility with these testing approaches:

ul.li: TypeScript Clients: Ensure generated clients work without modifications
Excel Add-ins: Test Office.js integrations and custom function calls
React/Angular Apps: Verify existing HTTP service layers continue working
Mobile Apps: Test native HTTP clients and authentication flows

body.p: Axis2 OpenAPI services can replace backends built with various frameworks:
The Axis2 OpenAPI integration is designed for enterprise performance and scalability:

ul.li: JSON Processing: Choice of Moshi, Gson, or streaming formatters — each with HTTP/2-enhanced variants for large payloads
HTTP Caching: Specification responses carry a short Cache-Control max-age, and static Swagger UI resources a longer one
Memory Management: Streaming support for large request/response payloads
Schema Validation: Use OpenAPI schema validation for request/response verification
Error Handling: Implement consistent error response formats across all services
Authentication: Centralize token validation and user context management
Monitoring: Implement service health checks and performance metrics
Documentation: Keep OpenAPI schemas up-to-date with service changes

body.p: Ensure secure REST API implementation:

ul.li: Input Validation: Validate all request parameters and payloads
Authentication: Implement proper token validation and session management
CORS Policy: Configure appropriate CORS policies for production environments
HTTPS: Use HTTPS in production for secure data transmission
Rate Limiting: Implement rate limiting to prevent API abuse

body.p: Common issues and solutions when implementing OpenAPI REST services:
If the OpenAPI module fails to load:

ol.li: Verify the module is included in axis2.xml: <module ref="openapi" />
Check that the openapi .mar file is present in the modules directory
Review server logs for initialization errors

body.p: If Swagger UI is not accessible:

ol.li: Confirm openapi.swaggerUi.enabled is not set to false
Check that a servlet delegating to SwaggerUIHandler is mapped at /swagger-ui
If the page loads but stays blank, check that the browser can reach the Swagger UI CDN

body.p: When replacing existing backends:

ol.li: Compare request/response formats using API testing tools
Verify custom header handling and authentication patterns
Test with actual frontend applications, not just cURL
Review error response formats and status codes

body.p: For performance optimization:

ol.li: Monitor memory usage with large JSON payloads
Check database connection pooling and query optimization

body.p: For additional support, contact the Axis2 community through the mailing lists or GitHub issues. The community welcomes contributions and feedback on the OpenAPI integration.
